sam_customer: Hey @alice_support, installing the Python SDK in editable mode with extras is giving an import error in our app after deploy. pip install -e .[async] succeeds but import redwood.api fails with ModuleNotFoundError.

alice_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact error + how you installed? quick check: are you using poetry or pip? :thinking_face:

sam_customer: Using poetry for dev, then we do `poetry build && pip install dist/redwood_sdk-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl` in CI. Locally we use `pip install -e .[async]`. Error from CI and local are the same.

sam_customer: Error:```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app/main.py", line 3, in <module>
    from redwood.api import RedwoodClient
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.api'
```

alice_support: thanks. can you run `python -c "import pkgutil, sys; print(sys.path); print(list(pkgutil.iter_modules()))"` and paste output? Also `pip show redwood-sdk` and `pip show redwood` if present.

sam_customer: quick outputs: `pip show redwood-sdk` shows name: redwood-sdk version: 0.1.0 location: /home/runner/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages`
`pip show redwood` -> WARNING: Package(s) not found: redwood
`ls -la /home/runner/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages | grep redwood` -> `redwood_sdk-0.1.0.dist-info` and `redwood_sdk` directory, no top-level `redwood` package.

sam_customer: Our code imports `from redwood.api import RedwoodClient` — SDK prior releases used `redwood` top-level package, but new wheel installs top-level package `redwood_sdk` instead. This may be the mismatch. We used extras expecting same module path.

alice_support: aha that explains it — packaging/name mismatch between import path and distribution name. can you share your pyproject.toml snippet?

sam_customer: snippet:```
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Redwood client"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]
[tool.poetry.extras]
async = ["httpx[http2]"]
```

alice_support: ok — your package is published/installed as `redwood_sdk` module, but your application imports `redwood`. there are two ways to fix: (1) change the package's top-level module to `redwood` (rename package directory or configure `packages = [{ include = "redwood" }]`), or (2) change your app imports to `from redwood_sdk.api import RedwoodClient`. for backwards compatibility we can also add a small shim package `redwood/__init__.py` that imports from `redwood_sdk`.

matt_engineer: adding to this — editable installs + symlinked projects can hide namespace-package issues. If you want the wheel to expose `redwood` while project dir is `redwood_sdk`, set `package-dir = {"":"src"}` and name your package folder `redwood` under `src/`. Or in pyproject you can set `packages = [ { include = "redwood", from = "src" } ]`.

sam_customer: we do have a `src/` layout but our folder is `src/redwood_sdk/` because we wanted to avoid top-level name conflict with an internal package named `redwood`. Ideally the distro would be `redwood` but we couldn't due to internal repo. Any workaround?

alice_support: workaround without renaming: create a tiny compatibility package in `src/redwood/__init__.py` that imports from `redwood_sdk`:```python
# src/redwood/__init__.py
from importlib import import_module
_api = import_module('redwood_sdk.api')
from _api import *
```
That will let `import redwood.api` work. Then rebuild wheel.

devex_bot: note: adding a shim is a valid short-term fix but careful with namespace packages and __all__ surface. Consider tests to ensure both import paths resolve.

sam_customer: tried shim, rebuilt, CI green. But we still see failures in editable dev env: `pip install -e .[async]` didn't create `redwood` entry, only `redwood_sdk` folder. Any ideas?

matt_engineer: editable install creates an .egg-link pointing at your project path. If shim exists in src/redwood it should be discoverable. Check for `easy-install.pth` lines and ensure your `src/` is referenced. run `python -c "import pkgutil; print(pkgutil.iter_importers('redwood'))"` to confirm. Also check for existing package named `redwood` in local path shadowing the shim.

sam_customer: found stray `redwood` directory at repo root from an early experiment — it was shadowing. Removed it and `pip install -e .[async]` now produces redwood import resolution OK locally. CI still uses wheel and had shim fix. All green. :tada:

alice_support: great! I'll mark this thread as solved but will add a short KB note for support articles: "Packaging mismatch: distribution vs import module name — shim and rename strategies". @matt_engineer can you follow up with a short guidance we can share?

matt_engineer: will draft a short doc with commands to audit packaging: `pip show`, `python -c "import importlib, pkgutil; print(importlib.util.find_spec('redwood'))"`, check egg-link/pth, and examples of shim code + pyproject examples.

sam_customer: really appreciate the quick help, saved our deploy.

deploy_bot: deploy 2254322040: CI pipeline passed for commit abc123 — promoted to staging.

alice_support: closing thread. If you hit regressions, re-open or ping #support. :slightly_smiling_face:
